newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business outlook improves - BOJ survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan business outlook improves - BOJ survey.

text.p: Major Japanese manufacturing firms grew cheerier in June and remained significantly more optimistic than their non-manufacturing colleagues, the Bank of Japan's closely watched "tankan" quarterly survey of corporate sentiment showed on Wednesday.

The diffusion index for manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven in June from plus two in March, when the previous survey was conducted. In March, the survey had forecast a manufacturers' diffusion index of minus one for June.
The diffusion index for major non-manufacturers, meanwhile, fell to minus seven in June from minus six in March. The June figure was as had been predicted in the March survey.

Economists' forecasts for the major manufacturers index had covered a wide range but the figure of plus seven was considerably stronger than analysts had expected. Japanese stocks jumped and the dollar fell by around one yen compared to late U.S. levels after the statistics were released, to trade at around 114 yen.
Financial markets have been anxious to see the tankan data for clues to when the Bank of Japan is likely to tighten its hyper-easy credit stance.

Japanese interest rates have been at rock-bottom levels since the central bank slashed its official discount rate, which it charges commercial banks, to a record low of 0.5 percent in September 1995 to keep the economy on track. Most economists have been expecting the Bank of Japan to wait until at least October and possibly until next year before raising interest rates, although some have said the central bank could move as early as August.
